| Project skills                | `.opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                                      |
| Global skills                 | `~/.config/opencode/skill(s)/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                                             |
| External skills (auto-loaded) | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`, `~/.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`                                                    |

Configs from each scope are deep-merged. Project overrides global. Unknown
top-level keys in `opencode.json` are rejected with `ConfigInvalidError`.

## opencode.json

Every field is optional.

```json
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "username": "string",
  "model": "provider/model-id",
  "small_model": "provider/model-id",
  "default_agent": "agent-name",
  "shell": "/bin/zsh",
  "logLevel": "DEBUG" | "INFO" | "WARN" | "ERROR",
  "share": "manual" | "auto" | "disabled",
  "autoupdate": true | false | "notify",
  "snapshot": true,
  "instructions": ["AGENTS.md", "docs/style.md"],

  "skills": {
    "paths": [".opencode/skills", "/abs/path/to/skills"],
    "urls": ["https://example.com/.well-known/skills/"]
  },

  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and documentation conventions"
    },
    "sdk": {
      "repository": "owner/sdk",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for SDK implementation details",
      "hidden": true
    }
  },

  "agent": {
    "my-agent": {
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "description": "...",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny" }
    }
  },

  "command": {
    "deploy": { "description": "...", "template": "..." }
  },

  "provider": {
    "anthropic": { "options": { "apiKey": "..." } }
  },
  "disabled_providers": ["openai"],
  "enabled_providers": ["anthropic"],

  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": {}
    },
    "remote-thing": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer ..." }
    }
  },

  "plugin": [
    "opencode-gemini-auth",
    "opencode-foo@1.2.3",
    "./local-plugin.ts",
    ["opencode-bar", { "option": "value" }]
  ],

  "permission": {
    "edit": "deny",
    "bash": { "git *": "allow", "*": "ask" }
  },

  "formatter": false,
  "lsp": false,

  "experimental": {
    "primary_tools": ["edit"],
    "mcp_timeout": 30000
  },

  "tool_output": { "max_lines": 200, "max_bytes": 8192 },

  "compaction": { "auto": true, "tail_turns": 15 }
}
```

Shape notes worth being explicit about:

- `model` always carries a provider prefix: `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"`.
- `skills` is an object with `paths` and/or `urls`, not an array.
- `references` is an object keyed by alias. Each value is a local path, Git repository, or string shorthand.
- `agent` is an object keyed by agent name, not an array.
- `command` is an object keyed by command name, not an array.
- `plugin` is an array of strings or `[name, options]` tuples, not an object.
- `mcp[name].command` is an array of strings, never a single string. `type` is required.
- `permission` is either a string action or an object keyed by tool name.

## Skills

opencode's skill loader scans for `**/SKILL.md` inside skill directories. The
file is named `SKILL.md` exactly, and lives in its own folder named after the
skill:

```
.opencode/skills/my-skill/SKILL.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
name: my-skill
description: One sentence covering what this skill does AND when to trigger it. Front-load the literal keywords or filenames the user is likely to say.
---

# My Skill

(skill body in markdown: instructions, examples, references)
```

- `name` is required, lowercase hyphen-separated, up to 64 chars, and matches the folder name.
- `description` is effectively required: skills without one are filtered out and never surfaced to the model. Cover both _what_ the skill does and _when_ to use it. Write in third person ("Use when...", not "I help with..."). Front-load concrete trigger keywords and filenames; gate with "Use ONLY when..." if the skill should stay quiet on adjacent topics.
- Optional: `license`, `compatibility`, `metadata` (string-string map).

Register skills from non-default locations via `skills.paths` (scanned
recursively for `**/SKILL.md`) and `skills.urls` (each URL serves a list of
skills).

## References

References make local directories and Git repositories outside the active
project available as supporting context. Configure them under `references`,
keyed by the alias used in `@` autocomplete:

```json
{
  "references": {
    "docs": {
      "path": "../product-docs",
      "description": "Use for product behavior and terminology"
    },
    "effect": {
      "repository": "Effect-TS/effect",
      "branch": "main",
      "description": "Use for Effect implementation details"
    }
  }
}
```

Local `path` values may be relative to the declaring config, absolute, or use
`~/`. Git `repository` values accept Git URLs, host/path references, and GitHub
`owner/repo` shorthand; `branch` is optional. Both forms support optional
`description` and `hidden` fields.

- Only references with a `description` are advertised to agents in system context.
- `hidden: true` removes a reference from TUI `@` autocomplete only. It remains available to agents and by direct path.
- Reference directories are automatically allowed through the external-directory boundary; normal read/edit/tool permissions still apply.
- String shorthand is supported: use `"docs": "../docs"` for local paths or `"effect": "Effect-TS/effect"` for Git repositories.

## Agents

Two ways to define an agent. Use the file form for anything non-trivial.

### Inline (in `opencode.json`)

```json
{
  "agent": {
    "my-reviewer": {
      "description": "Reviews PRs for style violations.",
      "mode": "subagent",
      "model": "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6",
      "permission": { "edit": "deny", "bash": "ask" },
      "prompt": "You are a strict PR reviewer..."
    }
  }
}
```

### File

```
.opencode/agent/my-reviewer.md      OR     .opencode/agents/my-reviewer.md
```

```markdown
---
description: Reviews PRs for style violations.
mode: subagent
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
permission:
  edit: deny
  bash: ask
---

You are a strict PR reviewer. Focus on...
```

The file body becomes the agent's `prompt`. Do not also put `prompt:` in the
frontmatter.

`mode` is one of `"primary"`, `"subagent"`, `"all"`.

Allowed top-level frontmatter fields: `name, model, variant, description, mode,
hidden, color, steps, options, permission, disable, temperature, top_p`. Any
unknown field is silently routed into `options`.

To disable a built-in agent: `agent: { build: { disable: true } }`, or in a
file, `disable: true` in frontmatter.

`default_agent` must point to a non-hidden, primary-mode agent.

### Built-in agents

opencode ships with `build`, `plan`, `general`, `explore`. Hidden internal agents:
`compaction`, `title`, `summary`. To override a built-in's fields, define the
same key in `agent: { <name>: { ... } }`.

## Commands

opencode's command loader scans for `**/*.md` inside command directories. The
file is named after the command, and lives directly inside the `command` folder:

```
.opencode/command/deploy.md
```

Frontmatter:

```markdown
---
description: One sentence describing what the command does.
agent: build
model: anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6
---

(command body in markdown: the prompt opencode runs, with $ARGUMENTS for the user's input)
```

- `template` is the command body — everything below the frontmatter — and is required: it is the prompt opencode runs when the command is invoked. Do not also put a `template:` key in the frontmatter.
- `$ARGUMENTS` is replaced with everything the user typed after the command; `$1`, `$2`, … pull individual positional arguments.
- Optional: `description`, `agent`, `model`, `variant`, `subtask`.

## Plugins

`plugin:` is an array. Each entry is one of:

```json
"plugin": [
  "opencode-gemini-auth",            // npm spec, latest
  "opencode-foo@1.2.3",              // npm spec, pinned
  "./local-plugin.ts",               // file path, relative to the declaring config
  "file:///abs/path/plugin.js",      // file URL
  ["opencode-bar", { "key": "val" }] // tuple form with options
]
```

Auto-discovered plugins (no config entry needed): any `*.ts` or `*.js` file in
`.opencode/plugin/` or `.opencode/plugins/`.

A plugin module exports `default` (or any named export) of type
`Plugin = (input: PluginInput, options?) => Promise<Hooks>`. The export is a
function, not a plain object literal, and the function returns an object
(return `{}` if there is nothing to register).

```ts
import type { Plugin } from "@opencode-ai/plugin"

export default (async ({ client, project, directory, $ }) => {
  return {
    config: (cfg) => {
      // cfg is the live merged config; mutate fields here.
    },
    "tool.execute.before": async (input, output) => {
      // mutate output.args before the tool runs
    },
  }
}) satisfies Plugin
```

Hook surface (mutate `output` in place; return `void`):

- `event(input)`: every bus event
- `config(cfg)`: once on init with the merged config
- `chat.message`, `chat.params`, `chat.headers`
- `tool.execute.before`, `tool.execute.after`
- `tool.definition`
- `command.execute.before`
- `shell.env`
- `permission.ask`
- `experimental.chat.messages.transform`, `experimental.chat.system.transform`,
  `experimental.session.compacting`, `experimental.compaction.autocontinue`,
  `experimental.text.complete`

Special object-shaped (not callbacks): `tool: { my_tool: { ... } }`,
`auth: { ... }`, `provider: { ... }`.

## MCP servers

`mcp:` is an object keyed by server name. Each server is discriminated by
`type`:

```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "playwright": {
      "type": "local",
      "command": ["npx", "-y", "@playwright/mcp"],
      "enabled": true,
      "environment": { "BROWSER": "chromium" }
    },
    "github": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://...",
      "enabled": true,
      "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer {env:GITHUB_TOKEN}" }
    },
    "old-server": { "enabled": false }
  }
}
```

`command` is an array of strings. `environment` sets environment variables for
a local MCP server. `type` is required. Use `enabled: false` to
disable a server inherited from a parent config. String values such as header
tokens support `{env:VAR}` interpolation (and `{file:path}`); the shell-style
`${VAR}` is not substituted.

## Permissions

```json
"permission": {
  "edit": "deny",
  "bash": { "git *": "allow", "rm *": "deny", "*": "ask" },
  "external_directory": { "~/secrets/**": "deny", "*": "allow" }
}
```

Actions: `"allow"`, `"ask"`, `"deny"`.

Per-tool value forms: `"allow"` shorthand (treated as `{"*": "allow"}`), or an
object `{ pattern: action }`. Within an object, **insertion order matters**.
opencode evaluates the LAST matching rule, so put broad rules first and narrow
rules last.

`permission: "allow"` (a string at the top level) is shorthand for "allow
everything" and is rarely what the user wants.

Known permission keys: `read, edit, glob, grep, list, bash, task,
external_directory, todowrite, question, webfetch, websearch, lsp, doom_loop,
skill`. Some of these (`todowrite,
question, webfetch, websearch, doom_loop`) only accept a flat
action, not a per-pattern object.

`external_directory` patterns are filesystem paths (use `~/`, absolute paths,
or globs like `~/projects/**`).

Per-agent `permission:` overrides top-level `permission:`. Plan Mode lives on
the `plan` agent's permission ruleset (`edit: deny *`).

## Escape hatches

When a user's config is broken and opencode won't start, these env vars help:

- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PROJECT_CONFIG=1`: skip the project's local `opencode.json`
  and start from globals only. Run from the project directory, opencode loads,
  the user edits the broken file, then they restart without the flag.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG=/path/to/file.json`: load an additional explicit config.
- `OPENCODE_CONFIG_CONTENT='{"$schema":"https://opencode.ai/config.json"}'`:
  inject inline JSON as a final local-scope merge.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_DEFAULT_PLUGINS=1`: skip default plugins.
- `OPENCODE_PURE=1`: skip external plugins entirely.
- `OPENCODE_DISABLE_EXTERNAL_SKILLS=1`,
  `OPENCODE_DISABLE_CLAUDE_CODE_SKILLS=1`: skip the external skill scans under
  `~/.claude/` and `~/.agents/`.

## When proposing edits

- Validate against the schema before writing. If you are unsure of a field's
  exact shape, or the field is not covered in this skill, fetch
  `https://opencode.ai/config.json` and read the schema rather than guessing.
- Preserve `$schema` and any existing fields the user did not ask to change.
- For agent, command, skill, and plugin definitions, prefer creating new files
  in the correct location over inlining everything in `opencode.json`.
- If the user's existing config is malformed, point them at the env-var escape
  hatches above so they can edit from inside opencode without breaking their
  session.
- After saving any config change, remind the user to quit and restart opencode
  — running sessions keep using the already-loaded config.

60: export function topologicalSortBlocks(graph: WorkflowGraph): WorkflowBlock[] {
61:   const blockMap = new Map<string, WorkflowBlock>(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, b]));
62:   const inDegree = new Map<string, number>(graph.blocks.map((b) => [b.id, 0]));
63: 
64:   for (const edge of graph.edges) {
65:     if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
66:       inDegree.set(edge.target, inDegree.get(edge.target)! + 1);
67:     }
68:   }
69: 
70:   const queue: string[] = [];
71:   for (const [id, deg] of inDegree.entries()) {
72:     if (deg === 0) queue.push(id);
73:   }
74: 
75:   const sorted: WorkflowBlock[] = [];
76:   while (queue.length > 0) {
77:     const id = queue.shift()!;
78:     const block = blockMap.get(id);
79:     if (block) sorted.push(block);
80: 
81:     for (const edge of graph.edges.filter((e) => e.source === id)) {
82:       if (inDegree.has(edge.target)) {
83:         const deg = inDegree.get(edge.target)! - 1;
84:         inDegree.set(edge.target, deg);
85:         if (deg === 0) queue.push(edge.target);
86:       }
87:     }
88:   }
89: 
90:   if (sorted.length < graph.blocks.length) {
91:     throw new EngineError("The blocks on this workplace form a loop");
92:   }
93: 
94:   return sorted;
95: }

97: export function collectAllBlocks(graph: WorkflowGraph): WorkflowBlock[] {

99:   function recurse(g: WorkflowGraph) {
100:     for (const b of g.blocks) {
101:       blocks.push(b);
102:       if (b.inner) recurse(b.inner);
103:     }
104:   }
105:   recurse(graph);
106:   return blocks;
107: }

127: export function getDownstreamBlockIds(graph: WorkflowGraph, failedBlockId: string): Set<string> {
128:   const downstream = new Set<string>();
129:   const adj = new Map<string, string[]>();
130: 
131:   for (const b of graph.blocks) adj.set(b.id, []);
132:   for (const e of graph.edges) adj.get(e.source)?.push(e.target);
133: 
134:   const queue = [failedBlockId];
135:   while (queue.length > 0) {
136:     const curr = queue.shift()!;
137:     const neighbors = adj.get(curr) ?? [];
138:     for (const next of neighbors) {
139:       if (!downstream.has(next)) {
140:         downstream.add(next);
141:         queue.push(next);
142:       }
143:     }
144:   }
145: 
146:   return downstream;
147: }

4: /** Matches the core IPC contract; optional while an older bridge has no review method. */
5: export interface SplitterReviewApi {

15:   setState(patch: Partial<ReviewState>): void;

18: export async function saveSplitterCorrection(
19:   store: ReviewStore,
20:   api: SplitterReviewApi,
21:   runId: string,
22:   blockId: string,
23:   input: Review,
24: ) {
25:   const state = store.getState();
26:   if (state.busy) throw new Error("Wait for the current run action to finish.");
27:   try {
28:     const review = SplitterReview.parse(input);
29:     const report = reportForStep(state.run, blockId);
30:     if (state.run?.id !== runId || !report || !splitterReviewGate(state.run, blockId))
31:       throw new Error(
32:         "Routing corrections require an editable paused HIL gate upstream of continuation.",
33:       );
34:     if (review.expectedVersion !== report.reviews.length)
35:       throw new Error(
36:         "Review version changed. Read the latest saved report before correcting a route.",
37:       );
38:     for (const change of review.changes) {
39:       const assignment = report.assignments.find((item) => item.itemId === change.itemId);
40:       if (!assignment || !report.branches.some((branch) => branch.portId === change.toPortId))
41:         throw new Error("Choose an item and output from the saved report.");
42:       if (assignment.outputPortId === change.toPortId)
43:         throw new Error("Choose a different output.");
44:     }
45:     if (!api.reviewSplitter)
46:       throw new Error("Routing correction is not available in this app version.");
47:     store.setState({ busy: true, error: null });
48:     const saved = WorkflowRun.parse(await api.reviewSplitter(runId, blockId, review));
49:     const savedReport = reportForStep(saved, blockId);
50:     if (saved.id !== runId || !savedReport || savedReport.reviews.length <= review.expectedVersion)
51:       throw new Error(
52:         "The server did not return a persisted routing correction. Reload the run before retrying.",
53:       );
54:     const current = store.getState().run;
55:     // A pushed update can arrive before IPC returns. Never replace a newer persisted revision.
56:     if (
57:       current?.id === runId &&
58:       (reportForStep(current, blockId)?.reviews.length ?? 0) <= savedReport.reviews.length &&
59:       current.status === "waiting_for_review"
60:     )
61:       store.setState({ run: saved });
62:     return saved;
63:   } catch (err) {
64:     store.setState({ error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
65:     throw err;
66:   } finally {
67:     store.setState({ busy: false });
68:   }

1: import { DATA_KEYS, type PipelineData } from "@reqflow/core";
2: import { emptyMembership, emptyOutputs, evidenceIndex, primaryLayer, select } from "./evidence";
3: 
4: /**
5:  * Raw records are primary, even when an upstream envelope also contains findings/requirements.
6:  * Linked non-primary context follows each referenced record. A multi-record finding may appear on
7:  * multiple outputs, but its original references are never rewritten and primary records never copied.
8:  * Cross-output record links resolve through the run/report rather than duplicating classified records.
9:  */
10: export function selectRawOutputs(input: PipelineData, routes: Map<string, number>, count: number) {
11:   const outputs = emptyOutputs(count);
12:   const memberships = Array.from({ length: count }, emptyMembership);
13:   const recordPorts = new Map<string, Set<number>>();
14:   for (const record of input.records) {
15:     const port = routes.get(record.id);
16:     if (port === undefined || !memberships[port])
17:       throw new Error(`AI Splitter missing raw route for ${record.id}`);
18:     memberships[port]!.records.add(record.id);
19:     memberships[port]!.sources.add(record.sourceId);
20:     recordPorts.set(record.id, new Set([port]));
21:   }
22:   let crossBranchEvidence = false;
23:   let unavailableReferenceCount = 0;
24:   const index = evidenceIndex(input, () => {
25:     unavailableReferenceCount++;
26:   });
27:   const fallback = input.records.length
28:     ? [...routes.values()].reduce((min, port) => Math.min(min, port), count - 1)
29:     : count - 1;
30:   for (const key of ["findings", "themes", "requirements"] as const) {
31:     for (const item of input[key]) {
32:       const closure = index.closure(key, item.id);
33:       const ports = new Set([...closure.records].flatMap((id) => [...(recordPorts.get(id) ?? [])]));
34:       if (ports.size > 1) crossBranchEvidence = true;
35:       if (!ports.size) ports.add(fallback);
36:       for (const port of ports) {
37:         for (const dependency of DATA_KEYS) {
38:           if (dependency === "records") continue;
39:           for (const id of closure[dependency]) memberships[port]![dependency].add(id);
40:         }
41:       }
42:     }
43:   }
44:   const referencedSources = new Set(memberships.flatMap((m) => [...m.sources]));
45:   for (const source of input.sources)
46:     if (!referencedSources.has(source.id)) memberships[fallback]!.sources.add(source.id);
47:   for (const [i, membership] of memberships.entries()) {
48:     // Keep envelope extensions even on empty outputs, and keep all original entity objects.
49:     outputs[`out-${i}`] = select(input, membership);
50:   }
51:   return { outputs, crossBranchEvidence, unavailableReferenceCount };
52: }
53: 
54: /** Evidence-free new modes preserve non-record envelopes once; no provisional customer demand. */
55: export function selectWithoutRecords(input: PipelineData, count: number) {
56:   const outputs = Object.fromEntries(
57:     Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => [`out-${i}`, select(input, emptyMembership())]),
58:   );
59:   const layer = primaryLayer(input) ?? "sources";
60:   outputs[`out-${count - 1}`] = input;
61:   return { outputs, layer };
62: }
</content>

2: import { Finding, Theme } from "./finding";
3: import { Requirement } from "./requirement";

5: 
6: /**
7:  * The single envelope that flows along every workflow edge (n8n-style: one input, one output).
8:  * A node reads the keys it `consumes` and returns the envelope with the keys it `produces` updated.
9:  */
10: export const DATA_KEYS = ["sources", "records", "findings", "themes", "requirements"] as const;
11: export const DataKey = z.enum(DATA_KEYS);
12: export type DataKey = z.infer<typeof DataKey>;
13: 
14: export const PipelineData = z.object({
15:   sources: z.array(Source),
16:   records: z.array(SourceRecord),
17:   findings: z.array(Finding),
18:   themes: z.array(Theme),
19:   requirements: z.array(Requirement),
20: });
21: export type PipelineData = z.infer<typeof PipelineData>;
22: 
23: export function emptyPipelineData(): PipelineData {
24:   return { sources: [], records: [], findings: [], themes: [], requirements: [] };
25: }
26: 
27: function mergeById<T extends { id: string }>(lists: T[][]): T[] {
28:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
29:   for (const list of lists) for (const item of list) byId.set(item.id, item);
30:   return [...byId.values()];
31: }
32: 
33: /**
34:  * How the engine combines several incoming edges into one node input:
35:  * concatenate per key and de-duplicate by `id`; a later input wins (order = edge order),
36:  * first-seen position is kept so output order stays stable.
37:  */
38: export function mergePipelineData(...parts: PipelineData[]): PipelineData {
39:   return {
40:     sources: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.sources)),
41:     records: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.records)),
42:     findings: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.findings)),
43:     themes: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.themes)),
44:     requirements: mergeById(parts.map((p) => p.requirements)),
45:   };
46: }
47: 
48: export function countPipelineData(data: PipelineData): Record<DataKey, number> {
49:   return {
50:     sources: data.sources.length,
51:     records: data.records.length,
52:     findings: data.findings.length,
53:     themes: data.themes.length,
54:     requirements: data.requirements.length,

7: 
8: /** Small request seam for offline tests; it does not expose tools, storage, or credentials discovery. */
9: export interface MastraAgentConfig {
10:   id: string;
11:   name: string;
12:   instructions: string;
13:   model: { providerId: "anthropic"; modelId: string; apiKey: string };
14:   maxRetries: 0;
15:   errorProcessorDefaults: false;
16: }
17: 
18: export interface MastraGenerateOptions {
19:   abortSignal?: AbortSignal;
20:   maxSteps: 1;
21:   modelSettings: { temperature: number; maxOutputTokens: number; maxRetries: 0 };
22:   structuredOutput?: {
23:     schema: z.ZodType<unknown>;
24:     errorStrategy: "strict";
25:     logger: IMastraLogger;
26:   };
27: }
28: 
29: export interface MastraGenerateResult {
30:   object?: unknown;
31:   text?: string;
32:   finishReason?: string;
33:   response?: { modelId?: string };
34:   error?: unknown;
35:   usedFallbackValue?: boolean;
36: }
37: 
38: export interface MastraAgent {
39:   generate(prompt: string, options: MastraGenerateOptions): Promise<MastraGenerateResult>;
40: }
41: 
42: export type MastraAgentFactory = (config: MastraAgentConfig) => MastraAgent;
43: 
44: export interface MastraLlmClientOptions extends LlmClientOptions {
45:   /** Replaces only Agent construction/generation; production uses the standalone Mastra Agent. */
46:   createAgent?: MastraAgentFactory;
47: }
48: 
49: const createAgent: MastraAgentFactory = (config) => {
50:   // Do not attach a Mastra instance: no tracing, memory, storage, tools, or source logging.
51:   const agent = new Agent(config);
52:   agent.__setLogger(noopLogger);
53:   return {
54:     generate: (prompt, options) =>
55:       options.structuredOutput
56:         ? agent.generate(prompt, { ...options, structuredOutput: options.structuredOutput })
57:         : agent.generate(prompt, { ...options, structuredOutput: undefined }),
58:   };
59: };
60: 
61: /** Provider errors can contain request bodies and credentials; expose only a numeric HTTP status. */
62: function providerError(error: unknown): Error {
63:   let current = error;
64:   for (let depth = 0; depth < 5 && current && typeof current === "object"; depth++) {
65:     const { statusCode, cause } = current as { statusCode?: unknown; cause?: unknown };
66:     if (
67:       typeof statusCode === "number" &&
68:       Number.isInteger(statusCode) &&
69:       statusCode >= 400 &&
70:       statusCode <= 599
71:     ) {
72:       return new Error(`Mastra Anthropic request failed (HTTP ${statusCode})`);
73:     }
74:     current = cause;
75:   }
76:   return new Error(
77:     "Mastra Anthropic generation failed; check model configuration, connectivity, or provider response.",
78:   );
79: }
80: 
81: /** Internal Anthropic provider; the public factory validates settings and reuses the existing mock. */
82: export function createMastraProvider(
83:   config: Settings["llm"],
84:   options: MastraLlmClientOptions,
85: ): LlmClient {
86:   const apiKey = options.apiKey?.trim();
87:   if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Anthropic API key is required; supply it from the secret store.");
88:   // Mastra's model router has no fetch option. Never silently ignore a caller's test transport.
89:   if (options.fetch && !options.createAgent) {
90:     throw new Error(
91:       "Inject createAgent for offline Mastra tests; use createLlmClient for fetch overrides.",
92:     );
93:   }
94:   const factory = options.createAgent ?? createAgent;
95: 
96:   async function generate(request: LlmTextRequest, schema?: z.ZodType<unknown>) {
97:     request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
98:     const checked = Request.parse(request);
99:     let result: MastraGenerateResult;
100:     try {
101:       result = await cancellable(() => {
102:         const agent = factory({
103:           id: "reqflow-llm",
104:           name: "ReqFlow LLM",
105:           instructions: checked.system ?? "",
106:           model: {
107:             providerId: "anthropic",
108:             modelId: checked.tier === "fast" ? config.fastModel : config.model,
109:             apiKey: apiKey!,
110:           },
111:           maxRetries: 0,
112:           // Mastra stability processors otherwise retry independently of model maxRetries.
113:           errorProcessorDefaults: false,
114:         });
115:         return agent.generate(checked.prompt, {
116:           abortSignal: request.signal,
117:           maxSteps: 1,
118:           modelSettings: { temperature: config.temperature, maxOutputTokens: 8192, maxRetries: 0 },
119:           ...(schema
120:             ? { structuredOutput: { schema, errorStrategy: "strict" as const, logger: noopLogger } }
121:             : {}),
122:         });
123:       }, request.signal);
124:       if (result.error) throw result.error;
125:     } catch (error) {
126:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
127:       throw providerError(error);
128:     }
129:     if (result.finishReason !== "stop" || result.usedFallbackValue) {
130:       throw new Error(
131:         "Mastra Anthropic response is incomplete, refused, or substituted; no output was accepted.",
132:       );
133:     }
134:     const model = z.string().min(1).parse(result.response?.modelId);
135:     return { result, model };
136:   }
137: 
138:   return {
139:     async generateObject(request) {
140:       const { result, model } = await generate(request, request.schema);
141:       if (result.object === undefined)
142:         throw new Error("Mastra Anthropic structured response is missing its object.");
143:       // Mastra validation is not a substitute for the caller's original Zod refinements.
144:       const object = request.schema.parse(result.object);
145:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
146:       return { object, model };
147:     },
148:     async generateText(request) {
149:       const { result, model } = await generate(request);
150:       const text = z.string().min(1).parse(result.text);
151:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
152:       return { text, model };
153:     },
154:   };

# AGENTS.md — read this first

## What we're building

**ReqFlow** is a hackathon prototype for the BMW challenge _"AI for Product Decision Making"_: a
**native desktop app for Windows, macOS and Linux** (Electron, not a web app) with three tabs. On
**Data Flow**, an n8n-style flow of **building blocks** (Custom, Raw, Research, AI Filter, AI Splitter,
HIL, Add to Car; some expand into their own inner workplace) turns customer and market data into
prioritized, evidence-linked car requirements. The **Car** tab shows them for the PM to review, and
**Settings** configures the app, global parameters and collaboration. Full spec: [PRODUCT.md](PRODUCT.md). Your task: [docs/WORKSTREAMS.md](docs/WORKSTREAMS.md).
Current state and handoffs: [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md).

## The challenge in brief (from `context/`)

- **Goal:** help BMW product managers define, justify and prioritize **customer-facing requirements
  for the successor** of an existing vehicle, thinking **3–5 years ahead**. The PM stays in control of
  every decision.
- **Vehicles and markets:** the 1, 5 or 7 Series, in Europe, China or the US. Demo **one derivative in one
  market** (ours: 1 Series F70, EU), but don't build a one-off.
- **BMW provides, per vehicle:** customer feedback, equipment data, sales volumes and a customer study.
  We may add web sources such as competitors, reviews and market or technology trends.
- **The app must:** ingest the data and enrich it from the web → extract signals (complaints, unmet needs,
  competitor advantages, trends), **each linked to its sources** → derive clear, actionable, realistic
  requirements → prioritize them with explainable logic → let the PM approve, reject, edit or challenge
  them → record everything in an **audit trail** (who or what, when, and why).
- **Each requirement needs:** a unique ID, an actionable description, linked findings and sources, a
  priority or score, the prioritization rationale, an evidence level, assumptions and uncertainties, and
  a decision status.
- **In scope:** features, equipment, comfort, space, usability, infotainment and digital services,
  design and quality perception, driving experience, range and charging as the customer experiences them,
  and variants and packages. **Out of scope:** regulatory and homologation topics, engineering specs, and
  pricing or business cases (rough effort may be used as a priority factor).
- **Judges value:** trustworthy sources, transparent reasoning, thoughtful prioritization, honest
  handling of uncertainty and **conflicting evidence**, and focus on customer value. Depth in one area
  beats shallow coverage of everything.
- **BMW process we mirror:** situation analysis → structure and context (classify, cluster, dedupe) →
  requirements definition (measurable targets and acceptance criteria) → prioritization (customer and
  business) → documentation and tracking. _"From 1 billion findings to 1,000 requirements to one car."_

## Rules for every agent

1. **Stay in your lane.** Edit only the paths your workstream owns (see WORKSTREAMS.md). Do you need
   something changed elsewhere? Write it in your final report instead of editing it yourself.
2. **`packages/core` is the contract.** Build against it and don't change it on your own. If you need a
   contract change, propose it in your final report. The lead merges contract changes.
3. **No real data in git, logs or transcripts.** BMW files go in `data/raw/` (gitignored). Entire
   publishes session transcripts, so when you inspect them, print only structure and counts (sheet
   and column names, row counts), never cell values, and never send them to delegated agents.
   Committed tests use synthetic data (`@reqflow/core/fixtures`, `data/samples/`). Never commit or
   print API keys.
4. **No silent failures.** Validate inputs with the Zod schemas, throw clear errors, and never invent
   sources or evidence. Every finding needs a verbatim excerpt.
5. **AI never decides.** Only a human sets `approved`, `rejected` or `deferred`. Every change to a
   requirement writes an AuditEvent.
6. **Prove it works.** Add colocated `*.test.ts` files. Before you report done, run
   `npm run typecheck && npm test` from the repo root. For UI work, also run `npm run smoke` and look at
   the screenshots in `apps/desktop/out/smoke/`.
7. **Respect the process split.** UI code (renderer) has no Node, no `fs` and no network. It talks to the
   main process only through `api` from `@/lib/api` (contract: `packages/core/src/ipc.ts`). Data, AI

8. **Sessions are tracked with [Entire](https://github.com/entireio/cli).** Commit with plain `git`.
   Entire attaches your session to each commit as a checkpoint and pushes it on `git push`. Don't

1: import { SplitterReview, WorkflowRun, type SplitterReview as Review } from "@reqflow/core";
2: import { reportForStep, splitterReviewGate } from "./splitter-view";
3: 
4: /** Matches the core IPC contract; optional while an older bridge has no review method. */
5: export interface SplitterReviewApi {
6:   reviewSplitter?: (runId: string, blockId: string, review: Review) => Promise<WorkflowRun>;
7: }
8: interface ReviewState {
9:   run: WorkflowRun | null;
10:   busy: boolean;
11:   error: string | null;
12: }
13: interface ReviewStore {
14:   getState(): ReviewState;
15:   setState(patch: Partial<ReviewState>): void;
16: }
17: 
18: export async function saveSplitterCorrection(
19:   store: ReviewStore,
20:   api: SplitterReviewApi,
21:   runId: string,
22:   blockId: string,
23:   input: Review,
24: ) {
25:   const state = store.getState();
26:   if (state.busy) throw new Error("Wait for the current run action to finish.");
27:   try {
28:     const review = SplitterReview.parse(input);
29:     const report = reportForStep(state.run, blockId);
30:     if (state.run?.id !== runId || !report || !splitterReviewGate(state.run, blockId))
31:       throw new Error(
32:         "Routing corrections require an editable paused HIL gate upstream of continuation.",
33:       );
34:     if (review.expectedVersion !== report.reviews.length)
35:       throw new Error(
36:         "Review version changed. Read the latest saved report before correcting a route.",
37:       );
38:     for (const change of review.changes) {
39:       const assignment = report.assignments.find((item) => item.itemId === change.itemId);
40:       if (!assignment || !report.branches.some((branch) => branch.portId === change.toPortId))
41:         throw new Error("Choose an item and output from the saved report.");
42:       if (assignment.outputPortId === change.toPortId)
43:         throw new Error("Choose a different output.");
44:     }
45:     if (!api.reviewSplitter)
46:       throw new Error("Routing correction is not available in this app version.");
47:     store.setState({ busy: true, error: null });
48:     const saved = WorkflowRun.parse(await api.reviewSplitter(runId, blockId, review));
49:     const savedReport = reportForStep(saved, blockId);
50:     if (saved.id !== runId || !savedReport || savedReport.reviews.length <= review.expectedVersion)
51:       throw new Error(
52:         "The server did not return a persisted routing correction. Reload the run before retrying.",
53:       );
54:     const current = store.getState().run;
55:     // A pushed update can arrive before IPC returns. Never replace a newer persisted revision.
56:     if (
57:       current?.id === runId &&
58:       (reportForStep(current, blockId)?.reviews.length ?? 0) <= savedReport.reviews.length &&
59:       current.status === "waiting_for_review"
60:     )
61:       store.setState({ run: saved });
62:     return saved;
63:   } catch (err) {
64:     store.setState({ error: err instanceof Error ? err.message : String(err) });
65:     throw err;
66:   } finally {
67:     store.setState({ busy: false });
68:   }
69: }
</content>

23:   }

29: export async function dispatch(

31:   namespace: string,
32:   method: string,
33:   args: unknown[],

43:     };

70:     portId: `out-${i}`,
71:     min: (100 * (count - i - 1)) / count,
72:     max: (100 * (count - i)) / count,
73:   }));
74: }
75: /** Inclusive lower bounds, exclusive upper bounds except 100; no quantiles or tie splitting. */
76: export function demandBand(score: number | null, count: number): number {
77:   if (score === null) return count - 1;
78:   for (const [i, band] of thresholds(count).entries()) if (score >= band.min) return i;
79:   return count - 1;
80: }
81: export function bandLabels(count: number): string[] {
82:   if (count === 2) return ["High", "Low"];
83:   if (count === 3) return ["High", "Medium", "Low"];
84:   if (count === 5) return ["Very High", "High", "Medium", "Low", "Very Low"];
85:   return thresholds(count).map((t) => `Demand ${format(t.min)}–${format(t.max)}`);
86: }
87: function format(value: number): string {
88:   return Number(value.toFixed(2)).toString();
89: }
90: 
91: /**
92:  * Demand is CODE ONLY: F=100*support/max_support, I=mean available supporting unit impacts,
93:  * score=0.7F+0.3I. Each unit contributes once; reimported evidence observations add no impact weight.
94:  * No available supporting impact means null I/contribution/score, never a fabricated zero.
95:  */
96: export function calculateGroups(
97:   plan: PlannedGroup[],
98:   signals: DemandSignal[],
99:   feedback: Set<string>,
100:   count: number,
101:   customerMode: boolean,
102: ): SplitterGroup[] {
103:   const summaries = plan.map((group) =>
104:     summarizeUnits(
105:       signals.filter((s) => s.groupId === group.id),
106:       feedback,
107:     ),
108:   );
109:   const counts = summaries.map(stanceCounts);
110:   const maxSupport = Math.max(0, ...counts.map((c) => c.support));
111:   return plan.map((group, i) => {
112:     const units = summaries[i]!;
113:     const impact = mean(
114:       [...units.values()].flatMap((u) =>
115:         u.stance === "support" && u.impact !== null ? [u.impact] : [],
116:       ),
117:     );
118:     const frequency = maxSupport > 0 ? (100 * counts[i]!.support) / maxSupport : null;
119:     const frequencyContribution = frequency === null ? null : 0.7 * frequency;
120:     const impactContribution = impact === null ? null : 0.3 * impact;
121:     const score =
122:       frequencyContribution === null || impactContribution === null
123:         ? null
124:         : Math.min(100, Math.max(0, frequencyContribution + impactContribution));
125:     const missingImpacts = [...units.values()].filter(
126:       (u) => u.stance === "support" && u.impact === null,
127:     ).length;
128:     return {
129:       id: group.id,
130:       label: group.label,
131:       description: group.description,
132:       outputPortId: `out-${customerMode ? demandBand(score, count) : i}`,
133:       ...counts[i]!,
134:       frequency,
135:       impact,
136:       frequencyContribution,
137:       impactContribution,
138:       score,
139:       scoreOrigin: score === null ? "not_computed" : "calculated",
140:       confidence: mean(
141:         [...units.values()].flatMap((u) => (u.confidence === null ? [] : [u.confidence])),
142:       ),
143:       assumptions: [
144:         "Frequency measures distinct feedback entries, not people or population prevalence.",
145:         "Within each feedback unit, canonical need plus verbatim excerpt identifies an impact observation; reimported copies add no impact weight.",
146:         ...(missingImpacts
147:           ? [
148:               `${missingImpacts} supporting feedback units have no expressed impact; available impacts only contribute to the mean.`,
149:             ]
150:           : []),
151:         ...(impact === null
152:           ? ["Expressed supporting impact is absent; customer demand score is not computed."]
153:           : []),
154:       ],
155:     };
156:   });
157: }
</content>

<path>../reqflow-ws7-ai-splitter/packages/blocks/src/raw/research-json.ts</path>
<content>
1: import {
2:   DATA_KEYS,
3:   Finding,
4:   PipelineData,
5:   Requirement,
6:   Source,
7:   SourceRecord,
8:   Theme,
9:   type DataKey,
10:   type StoredFile,
11: } from "@reqflow/core";
12: 
13: const MAX_JSON_BYTES = 16 * 1024 * 1024;
14: const schemas = {
15:   sources: Source,
16:   records: SourceRecord,
17:   findings: Finding,
18:   themes: Theme,
19:   requirements: Requirement,
20: };
21: 
22: /** Detect only declared JSON files; do not guess an envelope from CSV or spreadsheet contents. */
23: export function isResearchJsonFile(file: Pick<StoredFile, "name" | "mimeType">): boolean {
24:   const mime = file.mimeType.split(";", 1)[0]!.trim().toLowerCase();
25:   return /\.json$/i.test(file.name) || /^(application|text)\/(?:json|[^/\s]+\+json)$/.test(mime);
26: }
27: 
28: function fail(path: string, reason: string): never {
29:   // Paths and reasons are constructed here, never from data values or native parser messages.
30:   throw new Error(`Research JSON: ${path} ${reason}`);
31: }
32: 
33: function indexById<T extends { id: string }>(items: T[], layer: DataKey): Map<string, T> {
34:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
35:   for (const [index, item] of items.entries()) {
36:     if (byId.has(item.id)) fail(`${layer}[${index}].id`, "is a duplicate ID.");
37:     byId.set(item.id, item);
38:   }
39:   return byId;
40: }
41: 
42: /** Only explicit scalar IDs count; never infer an identity from arbitrary fields or wording. */
43: function identityField(record: SourceRecord, names: string[]): string | undefined {
44:   const fields = Object.entries(record.fields ?? {});
45:   for (const name of names) {
46:     for (const [key, value] of fields) {
47:       if (key.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, "") !== name.toLowerCase()) continue;
48:       if (typeof value === "string" && value.trim()) return value;
49:       if (typeof value === "number" && Number.isFinite(value)) return String(value);
50:     }
51:   }
52:   return undefined;
53: }
54: 
55: function checkIdentities(data: PipelineData): void {
56:   // A web URI identifies a document. Internal sources may share an upload URI across sheets.
57:   // No URL normalization is applied: queries and fragments can identify different evidence.
58:   const sourceUris = new Set<string>();
59:   for (const [index, source] of data.sources.entries()) {
60:     const uri = source.uri?.trim();
61:     if (source.origin !== "web" || !uri) continue;
62:     if (sourceUris.has(uri)) fail(`sources[${index}].uri`, "is a duplicate web source identity.");
63:     sourceUris.add(uri);
64:   }
65: 
66:   // Only an explicit original/comment ID in fields verifies a repeated entry. Scope it to the
67:   // source, provider and customer: local comment IDs may repeat across providers or customers.
68:   // Text and locators do not identify people or comments. Without an explicit original ID,
69:   // distinct core record IDs remain independent, even with identical text and locators.
70:   const recordIdentities = new Set<string>();
71:   for (const [index, record] of data.records.entries()) {
72:     const original = identityField(record, [
73:       "originalId",
74:       "originalRecordId",
75:       "originalCommentId",
76:       "providerRecordId",
77:       "reviewId",
78:       "feedbackId",
79:       "responseId",
80:       "commentId",
81:     ]);
82:     if (original === undefined) continue;
83:     const identity = JSON.stringify([
84:       record.sourceId,
85:       identityField(record, ["provider", "providerId", "providerName"]) ?? null,
86:       original,
87:       identityField(record, ["customerId", "respondentId", "authorId", "userId"]) ?? null,
88:     ]);
89:     if (recordIdentities.has(identity))
90:       fail(`records[${index}]`, "is a duplicate record identity.");
91:     recordIdentities.add(identity);
92:   }
93: }
94: 
95: function checkReferences(data: PipelineData): void {
96:   const sources = indexById(data.sources, "sources");
97:   const records = indexById(data.records, "records");
98:   const findings = indexById(data.findings, "findings");
99:   const themes = indexById(data.themes, "themes");
100:   indexById(data.requirements, "requirements");
101:   checkIdentities(data);
102: 
103:   const requireReference = (exists: boolean, path: string, layer: DataKey) => {
104:     if (!exists) fail(path, `must reference an item in ${layer}.`);
105:   };
106:   for (const [index, record] of data.records.entries()) {
107:     requireReference(sources.has(record.sourceId), `records[${index}].sourceId`, "sources");
108:   }
109:   for (const [index, finding] of data.findings.entries()) {
110:     if (finding.themeId !== undefined) {
111:       requireReference(themes.has(finding.themeId), `findings[${index}].themeId`, "themes");
112:     }
113:     for (const [evidenceIndex, evidence] of finding.evidence.entries()) {
114:       const path = `findings[${index}].evidence[${evidenceIndex}]`;
115:       requireReference(sources.has(evidence.sourceId), `${path}.sourceId`, "sources");
116:       if (evidence.recordId === undefined) continue; // Source-only evidence is allowed by core.
117:       const record = records.get(evidence.recordId);
118:       requireReference(record !== undefined, `${path}.recordId`, "records");
119:       if (record!.sourceId !== evidence.sourceId) {
120:         fail(`${path}.sourceId`, "does not match the linked record's source.");
121:       }
122:       if (!record!.text.includes(evidence.excerpt)) {
123:         fail(`${path}.excerpt`, "must be verbatim text from the linked record.");
124:       }
125:     }
126:   }
127:   for (const [index, theme] of data.themes.entries()) {
128:     for (const [linkIndex, id] of theme.findingIds.entries()) {
129:       requireReference(findings.has(id), `themes[${index}].findingIds[${linkIndex}]`, "findings");
130:     }
131:   }
132:   for (const [index, requirement] of data.requirements.entries()) {
133:     for (const field of ["findingIds", "conflictingFindingIds"] as const) {
134:       for (const [linkIndex, id] of requirement[field].entries()) {
135:         requireReference(
136:           findings.has(id),
137:           `requirements[${index}].${field}[${linkIndex}]`,
138:           "findings",
139:         );
140:       }
141:     }
142:     for (const [linkIndex, id] of requirement.sourceIds.entries()) {
143:       requireReference(
144:         sources.has(id),
145:         `requirements[${index}].sourceIds[${linkIndex}]`,
146:         "sources",
147:       );
148:     }
149:   }
150: }
151: 
152: /**
153:  * Accept a core PipelineData envelope or a structural Research dataset with sources and records.
154:  * Only absent findings/themes/requirements default to []; malformed supplied layers are errors.
155:  * Core schemas validate every layer, but their stripped parse output is deliberately discarded:
156:  * original objects, nested extensions, provenance and envelope metadata must survive unchanged.
157:  * Duplicate IDs/identities and dangling references fail instead of silently dropping evidence.
158:  * Errors contain only trusted schema fields and array indexes, never file contents or causes.
159:  */
160: export function parseResearchJson(bytes: Uint8Array): PipelineData & Record<string, unknown> {
161:   if (bytes.byteLength > MAX_JSON_BYTES) {
162:     throw new Error("Research JSON exceeds the 16 MiB file limit.");
163:   }
164:   let input: unknown;
165:   try {
166:     input = JSON.parse(new TextDecoder("utf-8", { fatal: true }).decode(bytes));
167:   } catch {
168:     throw new Error("Research JSON must contain valid UTF-8 JSON.");
169:   }
170:   if (
171:     !input ||
172:     typeof input !== "object" ||
173:     Array.isArray(input) ||
174:     !("sources" in input) ||
175:     !Array.isArray(input.sources) ||
176:     !("records" in input) ||
177:     !Array.isArray(input.records)
178:   ) {
179:     throw new Error("Research JSON must be an object with sources and records arrays.");
180:   }
181:   const data = { findings: [], themes: [], requirements: [], ...input };
182:   const validated = PipelineData.safeParse(data);
183:   if (!validated.success) {
184:     const issue = validated.error.issues[0]!;
185:     const layer = DATA_KEYS.find((key) => key === issue.path[0]);
186:     let path: string = layer ?? "envelope";
187:     if (layer && typeof issue.path[1] === "number") {
188:       path += `[${issue.path[1]}]`;
189:       const field = issue.path[2];
190:       if (typeof field === "string" && Object.hasOwn(schemas[layer].shape, field)) {
191:         path += `.${field}`;
192:       }
193:     }
194:     fail(path, `does not match the core schema (${issue.code}).`);
195:   }
196:   const original = data as PipelineData & Record<string, unknown>;
197:   checkReferences(original);
198:   return original;
199: }
</content>

18:  * assign@1 request: {contract, mode, instruction, needs, groups, items:[

12:       "category",
13:       "sentiment",
14:       "custom",

18:       .min(2)
19:       .max(10)

88: export function validateIds<T extends { id: string }>(
89:   items: T[],
90:   expected: string[],
91: ): Map<string, T> {
92:   const allowed = new Set(expected);
93:   const byId = new Map<string, T>();
94:   for (const [index, item] of items.entries()) {
95:     if (!allowed.has(item.id))
96:       throw new Error(`AI Splitter returned unknown assignment ID at response index ${index}`);
97:     if (byId.has(item.id))
98:       throw new Error(`AI Splitter returned duplicate assignment ID at response index ${index}`);
99:     byId.set(item.id, item);
100:   }
101:   const missing = expected.filter((id) => !byId.has(id));
102:   if (missing.length)
103:     throw new Error(`AI Splitter is missing assignments for ${missing.length} primary items`);
104:   return byId;
105: }

107: /** Bound both item count and prompt length; never truncate evidence silently. */
108: export function batches<T>(items: T[], payload: (batch: T[]) => unknown): T[][] {
109:   const result: T[][] = [];
110:   let current: T[] = [];
111:   for (const item of items) {
112:     const next = [...current, item];
113:     if (next.length > 20 || JSON.stringify(payload(next)).length > 96_000) {
114:       if (current.length) result.push(current);
115:       current = [item];
116:       if (JSON.stringify(payload(current)).length > 96_000) {
117:         throw new Error(
118:           "AI Splitter item and evidence exceed 96,000 prompt characters; reduce upstream item size.",
119:         );
120:       }
121:     } else current = next;
122:   }
123:   if (current.length) result.push(current);
124:   return result;
125: }

127: export async function generate<T>(ctx: BlockContext, request: LlmObjectRequest<T>) {
128:   ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
129:   let listener: () => void = () => {};
130:   const aborted = new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
131:     listener = () => reject(ctx.signal.reason);
132:     ctx.signal.addEventListener("abort", listener, { once: true });
133:   });
134:   try {
135:     const result = await Promise.race([
136:       ctx.llm.generateObject({ ...request, signal: ctx.signal }),
137:       aborted,
138:     ]);
139:     ctx.signal.throwIfAborted();
140:     return {
141:       object: request.schema.parse(result.object),
142:       model: z.string().min(1).parse(result.model),
143:     };
144:   } finally {
145:     ctx.signal.removeEventListener("abort", listener);
146:   }
147: }

7: import { z } from "zod";

10: import { createMastraProvider, type MastraLlmClientOptions } from "./mastra";
11: import { mockObject } from "./mock";
12: 
13: export type {
14:   MastraAgent,
15:   MastraAgentConfig,
16:   MastraAgentFactory,
17:   MastraGenerateOptions,
18:   MastraGenerateResult,
19:   MastraLlmClientOptions,
20: } from "./mastra";
21: 
22: export interface LlmClientOptions {
23:   /** Supplied by the main process secret store, never read from the environment. */
24:   apiKey?: string;
25:   /** Injectable transport for recorded, offline HTTP tests. */
26:   fetch?: typeof globalThis.fetch;
27: }
28: 
29: const Message = z.object({
30:   model: z.string().min(1),
31:   stop_reason: z.literal("end_turn"),
32:   content: z.array(z.object({ type: z.literal("text"), text: z.string() })).min(1),
33: });
34: 
35: /** Stateless standalone Mastra provider. Construction validates config but makes no model calls. */
36: export function createMastraLlmClient(
37:   settings: AppSettings["llm"],
38:   options: MastraLlmClientOptions = {},
39: ): LlmClient {
40:   const config = Settings.shape.llm.parse(settings);
41:   return config.provider === "mock"
42:     ? createLlmClient(config, options)
43:     : createMastraProvider(config, options);
44: }
45: 
46: /** Minimal Messages API client. No retries, secret discovery, SDK, or live calls at construction. */
47: export function createLlmClient(
48:   settings: AppSettings["llm"],
49:   options: LlmClientOptions = {},
50: ): LlmClient {
51:   const config = Settings.shape.llm.parse(settings);
52:   if (config.provider === "mock") {
53:     return {
54:       async generateObject(request) {
55:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
56:         const checked = Request.parse(request);
57:         const object = request.schema.parse(mockObject(checked.prompt));
58:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
59:         return { object, model: `mock:${checked.tier ?? "default"}` };
60:       },
61:       async generateText(request) {
62:         request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
63:         const checked = Request.parse(request);
64:         return {
65:           text: "[MOCK] Offline provider does not generate prose.",
66:           model: `mock:${checked.tier ?? "default"}`,
67:         };
68:       },
69:     };
70:   }
71: 
72:   const apiKey = options.apiKey?.trim();
73:   if (!apiKey) throw new Error("Anthropic API key is required; supply it from the secret store.");
74:   const fetch = options.fetch ?? globalThis.fetch;
75: 
76:   async function message(request: LlmTextRequest, schema?: Record<string, unknown>) {
77:     request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
78:     const checked = Request.parse(request);
79:     const body = {
80:       model: checked.tier === "fast" ? config.fastModel : config.model,
81:       max_tokens: 8192,
82:       temperature: config.temperature,
83:       ...(checked.system !== undefined ? { system: checked.system } : {}),
84:       messages: [{ role: "user", content: checked.prompt }],
85:       ...(schema ? { output_config: { format: { type: "json_schema", schema } } } : {}),
86:     };
87:     const result = await cancellable(async () => {
88:       const response = await fetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", {
89:         method: "POST",
90:         headers: {
91:           "content-type": "application/json",
92:           "anthropic-version": "2023-06-01",
93:           "x-api-key": apiKey!,
94:         },
95:         body: JSON.stringify(body),
96:         signal: request.signal,
97:       });
98:       // Error bodies can contain secrets or request text. Do not include them in errors/logs.
99:       if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Anthropic request failed (HTTP ${response.status})`);
100:       return Message.parse(await response.json());
101:     }, request.signal);
102:     return { text: result.content.map((part) => part.text).join(""), model: result.model };
103:   }
104: 
105:   return {
106:     async generateObject(request) {
107:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
108:       // Adapt transport constraints only; always validate the response with the original Zod schema.
109:       const jsonSchema = anthropicSchema(z.toJSONSchema(request.schema));
110:       const result = await message(request, jsonSchema);
111:       let raw: unknown;
112:       try {
113:         raw = JSON.parse(result.text);
114:       } catch {
115:         throw new Error("Anthropic structured response is not valid JSON");
116:       }
117:       const object = request.schema.parse(raw);
118:       request.signal?.throwIfAborted();
119:       return { object, model: result.model };
120:     },
121:     generateText: (request) => message(request),
122:   };
123: }

1: import { DATA_KEYS, type PipelineData } from "@reqflow/core";
2: import { emptyMembership, emptyOutputs, evidenceIndex, primaryLayer, select } from "./evidence";
3: 
4: /**
5:  * Raw records are primary, even when an upstream envelope also contains findings/requirements.
6:  * Linked non-primary context follows each referenced record. A multi-record finding may appear on
7:  * multiple outputs, but its original references are never rewritten and primary records never copied.
8:  * Cross-output record links resolve through the run/report rather than duplicating classified records.
9:  */
10: export function selectRawOutputs(input: PipelineData, routes: Map<string, number>, count: number) {
11:   const outputs = emptyOutputs(count);
12:   const memberships = Array.from({ length: count }, emptyMembership);
13:   const recordPorts = new Map<string, Set<number>>();
14:   for (const record of input.records) {
15:     const port = routes.get(record.id);
16:     if (port === undefined || !memberships[port])
17:       throw new Error(`AI Splitter missing raw route for ${record.id}`);
18:     memberships[port]!.records.add(record.id);
19:     memberships[port]!.sources.add(record.sourceId);
20:     recordPorts.set(record.id, new Set([port]));
21:   }
22:   let crossBranchEvidence = false;
23:   let unavailableReferenceCount = 0;
24:   const index = evidenceIndex(input, () => {
25:     unavailableReferenceCount++;
26:   });
27:   const fallback = input.records.length
28:     ? [...routes.values()].reduce((min, port) => Math.min(min, port), count - 1)
29:     : count - 1;
30:   for (const key of ["findings", "themes", "requirements"] as const) {
31:     for (const item of input[key]) {
32:       const closure = index.closure(key, item.id);
33:       const ports = new Set([...closure.records].flatMap((id) => [...(recordPorts.get(id) ?? [])]));
34:       if (ports.size > 1) crossBranchEvidence = true;
35:       if (!ports.size) ports.add(fallback);
36:       for (const port of ports) {
37:         for (const dependency of DATA_KEYS) {
38:           if (dependency === "records") continue;
39:           for (const id of closure[dependency]) memberships[port]![dependency].add(id);
40:         }
41:       }
42:     }
43:   }
44:   const referencedSources = new Set(memberships.flatMap((m) => [...m.sources]));
45:   for (const source of input.sources)
46:     if (!referencedSources.has(source.id)) memberships[fallback]!.sources.add(source.id);
47:   for (const [i, membership] of memberships.entries()) {
48:     // Keep envelope extensions even on empty outputs, and keep all original entity objects.
49:     outputs[`out-${i}`] = select(input, membership);
50:   }
51:   return { outputs, crossBranchEvidence, unavailableReferenceCount };
52: }
53: 
54: /** Evidence-free new modes preserve non-record envelopes once; no provisional customer demand. */
55: export function selectWithoutRecords(input: PipelineData, count: number) {
56:   const outputs = Object.fromEntries(
57:     Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => [`out-${i}`, select(input, emptyMembership())]),
58:   );
59:   const layer = primaryLayer(input) ?? "sources";
60:   outputs[`out-${count - 1}`] = input;
61:   return { outputs, layer };
62: }
